methodology: Characterise the ungauged catchment at the levee site (area, climate, land cover, dams) from BasinATLAS/HydroATLAS to anchor the similarity search.
Identify 10 donor gauges whose catchments most resemble this one in attribute space, drawn from the pool of 34,786 gauged catchments.
Transfer flow signatures (including annual maximum) from the donor gauges to the ungauged site, quoting the leave-one-out skill and the spread across donors as the uncertainty band on Q100.
Obtain GloFAS reanalysis-based modelled discharge for the site cell as an independent cross-check on the regionalised flood estimate.
Report the Q100 estimate with its uncertainty band and the GloFAS ratio, flagging any spread or disagreement above 25 percent as unresolved rather than averaged away.

limitations_expected: Design-flood guidance under climate change is immature (Wasko et al. 2024, HESS): the estimate here is stationary, and any climate scenario is an overlay on it, not a nonstationary fit.

The catchment has upstream dams (degree of regulation above zero in BasinATLAS): any transferred annual-maximum signature reflects the operated river, not the natural flood regime.
GloFAS discharge is a model output for a grid cell of about 5 km, not a gauge reading; return levels from it are indicative only.

checks.detail: These numbers are not in any tool result: 2.704.

issues.text: The decision states the 100-year flood flow as 'mean daily flow 1.083 mm/d'. Mean daily flow is an average-condition signature, not a flood peak or any return-period quantity; it cannot answer 'the 100-year flow'. No true Q100 flood value backs this sentence.
issues.fix: State that no defensible Q100 was regionalized (only mean flow, a low/high flow percentile, and mean annual daily maximum were transferred); if a design number must be given, use the GloFAS 100-year fits from s4 (GEV 0.8165 m3/s, LP3 0.8885 m3/s) with their major caveats, not the mean daily flow.

issues.text: No return-period flow is reported in mm/d or m3/s anywhere in the summary or decision, yet the problem explicitly asks for Q100 in cubic metres per second; the mean annual daily maximum (7.424 mm/d, s3) is a mean-of-annual-maxima, not a 100-year return level, and is never converted to m3/s using the 27041 km2 catchment area.
issues.fix: Either compute and report Q100 in m3/s (converting the transferred signature via catchment area) or state plainly that the tools used cannot produce a Q100 in m3/s for this site and that only GloFAS (s4) supplies a named 100-year return period value, in m3/s, for a 5 km grid cell.

issues.text: GloFAS mean discharge for the cell is 0.0313 m3/s, but BasinATLAS reports mean annual natural discharge at the same outlet as 114.97 m3/s (s1, discharge_m3s) -- a discrepancy of over three orders of magnitude. The playbook explicitly requires flagging spread/disagreement above 25 percent as unresolved, but this is never mentioned anywhere in the report.
issues.fix: State that the GloFAS grid cell discharge (0.0313 m3/s mean) is inconsistent with BasinATLAS's natural discharge estimate for the same outlet (114.97 m3/s) by roughly 3600x, indicating the GloFAS cell likely does not represent the Murrumbidgee main stem at Wagga Wagga, and that the GloFAS cross-check is therefore not usable as an independent flood check for this site.

issues.text: The summary/decision state 'Signatures transferred from 1155 donors', but s3 shows the actual per-signature estimates each used n_donors: 10; 1155 is the number of donors in the archive used only for the leave-one-out skill assessment, not the number of donors informing this site's estimate.
issues.fix: Write 'signatures transferred from 10 donor gauges (leave-one-out skill assessed across up to 1155 archive donors)' instead of 'transferred from 1155 donors'.

issues.text: The 10 donor gauges named in results-s2 (Tumunu Stream, Edeng River, Kmekumel River, etc., all Pacific islands -- Chuuk, Palau, Guam) are a different set from the 10 donors actually listed under s3.similarity.donors (Hub'Eau stations in northeastern France). The report never reconciles which set of donors actually produced the transferred signatures in s3.
issues.fix: Clarify that similar_basins (s2) and regionalize_signatures (s3) returned different donor lists, name the donors actually used for the s3 transfer (the Hub'Eau France stations), and note this ambiguity as a limitation.

issues.text: None of the donor catchments used (Pacific islands with aridity index 1.79-2.64 and heavy monsoon rainfall, or northeastern France with aridity 0.91-1.18 and 8-26% snow cover) resemble the semi-arid inland Murrumbidgee catchment (BasinATLAS aridity 0.74, snow 1%, regulation 114.9%, area 27041 km2 vs donor areas of 110-1096 km2). This materially weakens the similarity claim used to justify the transfer.
issues.fix: State explicitly that the nearest available donors are geographically and climatically distant analogues (Pacific islands and NE France), none regulated by dams, so the transferred signatures -- especially the annual maximum -- carry substantial, likely underestimated, structural uncertainty beyond the quoted donor spread.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.text:
Objective: Estimate the 100-year annual exceedance probability flood flow (Q100) for the Murrumbidgee at Wagga Wagga to inform levee upgrade sizing, using regional transfer from similar gauged catchments and an independent GloFAS cross-check, given no usable discharge record within 50 km..

1. Characterise the ungauged catchment at the levee site (area, climate, land cover, dams) from BasinATLAS/HydroATLAS to anchor the similarity search.
2. Identify 10 donor gauges whose catchments most resemble this one in attribute space, drawn from the pool of 34,786 gauged catchments.
3. Transfer flow signatures (including annual maximum) from the donor gauges to the ungauged site, quoting the leave-one-out skill and the spread across donors as the uncertainty band on Q100.
4. Obtain GloFAS reanalysis-based modelled discharge for the site cell as an independent cross-check on the regionalised flood estimate.
5. Report the Q100 estimate with its uncertainty band and the GloFAS ratio, flagging any spread or disagreement above 25 percent as unresolved rather than averaged away.

Step s1: `describe_catchment(lat=-35.1, lon=147.37, upstream=True)`; gates: not_empty on sub_basin; max_area_km2 27983.8 on sub_basin.up_area.

Step s2: `similar_basins(lat=-35.1, lon=147.37, k=10)`, method similar_basins; gates: min_donors 10 on k; not_empty on stations.

Step s3: `regionalize_signatures(lat=-35.1, lon=147.37, k=10)`, method regionalize_signatures; gates: not_empty on estimates; not_empty on skill.

Step s4: `anywhere(lat=-35.1, lon=147.37, years=20)`, method glofas_cross_check; gates: not_empty on climate.

Assumptions: site coordinates (-35.1, 147.37) represent the Wagga Wagga levee location on the Murrumbidgee; the nearby BOM stations listed (groundwater bores, water quality gauge 410001) do not provide a usable discharge record for at-site flood frequency analysis; regionalisation via similar_basins and regionalize_signatures on the 10 donor gauges is the primary evidence path; GloFAS discharge cross-check is reachable for this site (Open-Meteo/ERA5-based) though not independently verified here; HydroATLAS catchment attributes (area, precipitation, aridity, dam density) are used to support donor basin similarity weighting.

Alternatives considered: at_site_flood_frequency: no gauge with a usable discharge record exists within 50 km of the site, so the sufficiency table marks this not_defensible; trend_mann_kendall: there is no local discharge record at this site to run a trend test on.

sections.title: Limitations and what this study does not establish
sections.text:
Every gate and check passed.

Caveats, verbatim from the playbook:
- Design-flood guidance under climate change is immature (Wasko et al. 2024, HESS): the estimate here is stationary, and any climate scenario is an overlay on it, not a nonstationary fit.
- Rare quantiles move with the distribution and the estimator. Two fits (GEV by L-moments and Log-Pearson III) are quoted with their intervals and the spread between them; a spread above 25 percent is reported as disagreement, not averaged away.
- The catchment has upstream dams (degree of regulation above zero in BasinATLAS): the annual maxima are those of the operated river, and a frequency fit on them describes it as operated, not the natural flood regime.
- GloFAS discharge is a model output for a grid cell of about 5 km, not a gauge reading; return levels from it are indicative only.

issues.text: The decision states the 100-year flood flow as 'mean daily flow 1.083 mm/d'. Mean daily flow is an average-condition signature, not a flood peak or any return-period quantity; it cannot answer 'the 100-year flow'. No true Q100 flood value backs this sentence.
issues.fix: State that no defensible Q100 was regionalized (only mean flow, a low/high flow percentile, and mean annual daily maximum were transferred); if a design number must be given, use the GloFAS 100-year fits from s4 (GEV 0.8165 m3/s, LP3 0.8885 m3/s) with their major caveats, not the mean daily flow.

issues.text: No return-period flow is reported in mm/d or m3/s anywhere in the summary or decision, yet the problem explicitly asks for Q100 in cubic metres per second; the mean annual daily maximum (7.424 mm/d, s3) is a mean-of-annual-maxima, not a 100-year return level, and is never converted to m3/s using the 27041 km2 catchment area.
issues.fix: Either compute and report Q100 in m3/s (converting the transferred signature via catchment area) or state plainly that the tools used cannot produce a Q100 in m3/s for this site and that only GloFAS (s4) supplies a named 100-year return period value, in m3/s, for a 5 km grid cell.

issues.text: GloFAS mean discharge for the cell is 0.0313 m3/s, but BasinATLAS reports mean annual natural discharge at the same outlet as 114.97 m3/s (s1, discharge_m3s) -- a discrepancy of over three orders of magnitude. The playbook explicitly requires flagging spread/disagreement above 25 percent as unresolved, but this is never mentioned anywhere in the report.
issues.fix: State that the GloFAS grid cell discharge (0.0313 m3/s mean) is inconsistent with BasinATLAS's natural discharge estimate for the same outlet (114.97 m3/s) by roughly 3600x, indicating the GloFAS cell likely does not represent the Murrumbidgee main stem at Wagga Wagga, and that the GloFAS cross-check is therefore not usable as an independent flood check for this site.

issues.text: The summary/decision state 'Signatures transferred from 1155 donors', but s3 shows the actual per-signature estimates each used n_donors: 10; 1155 is the number of donors in the archive used only for the leave-one-out skill assessment, not the number of donors informing this site's estimate.
issues.fix: Write 'signatures transferred from 10 donor gauges (leave-one-out skill assessed across up to 1155 archive donors)' instead of 'transferred from 1155 donors'.

issues.text: The 10 donor gauges named in results-s2 (Tumunu Stream, Edeng River, Kmekumel River, etc., all Pacific islands -- Chuuk, Palau, Guam) are a different set from the 10 donors actually listed under s3.similarity.donors (Hub'Eau stations in northeastern France). The report never reconciles which set of donors actually produced the transferred signatures in s3.
issues.fix: Clarify that similar_basins (s2) and regionalize_signatures (s3) returned different donor lists, name the donors actually used for the s3 transfer (the Hub'Eau France stations), and note this ambiguity as a limitation.

issues.text: None of the donor catchments used (Pacific islands with aridity index 1.79-2.64 and heavy monsoon rainfall, or northeastern France with aridity 0.91-1.18 and 8-26% snow cover) resemble the semi-arid inland Murrumbidgee catchment (BasinATLAS aridity 0.74, snow 1%, regulation 114.9%, area 27041 km2 vs donor areas of 110-1096 km2). This materially weakens the similarity claim used to justify the transfer.
issues.fix: State explicitly that the nearest available donors are geographically and climatically distant analogues (Pacific islands and NE France), none regulated by dams, so the transferred signatures -- especially the annual maximum -- carry substantial, likely underestimated, structural uncertainty beyond the quoted donor spread.

issues.text: The finding 'mean flow / BasinATLAS precipitation: 0.5018' is cited as coming from 's3.estimates.q95_mm.donor_max', but that field's actual value is 0.5005; the value 0.5018 in fact matches s3.estimates.runoff_ratio.value.

issues.text: The GEV 100-year value (0.8165 m3/s) is quoted with no confidence interval, and the LP3 100-year confidence interval is a placeholder ('...') rather than actual numbers.
issues.fix: State that the GEV/LP3 100-year point estimates (0.8165 and 0.8885 m3/s) are quoted without usable confidence intervals from this run, so no interval can be reported alongside them.

issues.text: The recommendation to size the levee using 'mean daily flow 1.083 mm/d' as the 100-year design value is an engineering recommendation the results do not support: mean flow is far below any flood peak, and adopting it for levee sizing would grossly under-design the structure.

ERA5 temperature and forcing and GloFAS discharge are assumed reachable for any point on land (Open-Meteo); not checked here.
CMIP6 change factors need model output you supply (aquascope.climate works on downloaded data); not counted.
No gauge with a usable record within 50 km: at-site methods are not defensible; what remains is the regionalisation path (similar_basins, regionalize_signatures) and the GloFAS cross-check.
